transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what’s been going on that brought you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I really appreciate it, and I hope I'm not taking up time from patients who are, you know, really sick. 

I guess what brought me in is... well, my wife really wanted me to talk to someone. It's probably just a bit of stress, but I've noticed I just can't seem to keep my mind on one thing anymore. I'm a software developer, and lately, I'll be right in the middle of fixing a rendering bug, and... um... a Slack ping will pop up, or I'll notice a really interesting color pattern on the screen, or even just hear a siren outside. And it's like it just pulls me into a completely new idea before I can even finish the line of code I'm typing. 

I mean, the ideas I'm getting are actually really great, so I don't want to sound like I'm complaining! But I guess it's making it a little hard to actually finish my tasks. Is that... is that the kind of thing you usually help people with? Am I explaining that okay?
Have you noticed any periods where you felt unusually upbeat, irritable, or energized for at least a few days, even if it was accompanied by some of these racing ideas or distractions you mentioned?

Well, um... yeah, I suppose upbeat is a really good word for it. Honestly, most days lately I've just felt completely lit up. Like I'm just unstoppable. I've been building some incredible things, and it finally feels like Glendale has caught up with my vision, which is just an amazing feeling, you know? 

But, um... you mentioned being irritable. I... I guess I should admit, I have been a little short with people. Which I feel terrible about, I really do. It's just... my coworkers, or even my wife, they keep trying to slow me down with what they call process. And when you're moving that fast and seeing all the connections, it's hard to hit the brakes, so I... well, I have snapped at them a little hard a few times. 

I really don't like being that kind of guy, though, and I always feel bad after. I hope that doesn't make me sound awful. It's just passion for the work, right? Does that make sense?

Over the past week or so, have you had any days where your mood was so high or your energy was so intense that it was noticeably different from your usual self, even beyond just feeling upbeat or passionate about your work?

Well, um... I guess if I'm being completely honest, yeah, it's been a bit more than just upbeat. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm bragging or anything, but I've just been running on this... this constant current. 

Like, I'll wake up, and my brain is already going a mile a minute. I'm planning out new software features, and then I'm thinking about how to lay out the exhibitions for them, and then I'm writing the press angles in my head, and mapping out the code changes all at the same time. It's actually been incredibly productive! 

But... well, I suppose it is a lot different from my usual self. Sitting still just feels like I'm wasting the moment, you know? Like I have to keep moving or I'll lose all these brilliant ideas. I really hope that doesn't sound too crazy or like I'm losing touch with reality. I just want to do a good job. Is that... is that the kind of energy you're asking about?

Over the past week, have you had days where your mood was so high and your energy so intense that it felt like you didn’t need much sleep, and you were constantly driven to work on your ideas or projects without feeling tired?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I really don't want you to think I'm being irresponsible with my health or anything. I know how important rest is, especially at my age. 

I might stay up a little late sometimes because the code is just flowing and I'm really passionate about getting it right, but I definitely still feel tired eventually. I don't feel like I *don't* need sleep. I'm not, like, a machine or anything, and I always try to get to bed so my wife doesn't worry about me. 

I hope that's okay? I mean, I'm trying to be really careful not to overdo it and run myself into the ground, I promise. Does that answer your question all right?
Have you found yourself doing things that are risky or out of character lately, like spending a lot of money, taking on too many projects, or making big decisions without thinking them through?

Well, um... I guess... I mean, I really don't want you to think I'm reckless or anything. I always try to be responsible, especially with my family and my job. But... well, I suppose I have made a few decisions lately that were... maybe a little impulsive? 

I just... I saw this incredible opportunity for the project, and I wanted to make sure we capitalized on it. So I did spend some money that my wife and I hadn't exactly agreed on yet. Just on some GPUs, and some print materials and promo videos to really sell the vision. I know I should have talked to her first, and I feel awful about it, I really do. I'm going to make it right. 

And at work, um... I might have pushed a software update live without going through the final approval process. I know that sounds bad! It's just... waiting for another whole review cycle felt like letting the whole opportunity die, and I knew the code was solid. I just wanted to help the company succeed, you know? I hope you don't think I'm a bad person for doing that. I'm usually such a rule-follower, I promise. Does that make sense why I did it?

Have there been distinct periods of time—lasting at least a few days—where your mood was noticeably more elevated, irritable, or energized in a way that was clearly different from your usual non-depressed mood, even if you still felt tired sometimes or slept a bit?

Well, um... I guess if I look back at the past week or so, yes, there's definitely been a shift. I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm completely out of control, because I'm really trying my best here. But... yeah, most days recently, I've just felt this incredible spark. Like I'm lit up from the inside, and I'm just unstoppable. It finally feels like the rest of Glendale is catching up to the vision I've been building all this time. It's a really good feeling, honestly.

But... well, I suppose there is a downside, and I feel really bad admitting this. I know I should be more patient. It's just... when my wife or my coworkers try to slow me down, talking about "process" or needing to review things again... I've been snapping at them. And I mean snapping hard. I know it's wrong, and I always apologize, because I really don't want to be that kind of guy. I'm usually very easy to work with, I promise. It's just so frustrating when you can see the finish line and people keep putting up roadblocks, you know? 

I hope you don't think I'm just an angry person. I'm really trying to keep it in check. Is it normal to get a little irritable when you're just really focused on a big goal?

Would you say there have been at least four days in a row recently where your mood was clearly and consistently more elevated, irritable, or energized compared to how you usually feel when you’re not down?

Well, um... four days? I mean, I don't want to make it sound like it's this sudden, crazy thing that just happened out of nowhere. I've been feeling pretty good for a while now. 

Actually, it's been going on for about three months, I guess? Ever since my platform was selected for the Glendale showcase. It was such a huge honor, and I just... I really wanted to rise to the occasion, you know? So I've just been feeling really driven and focused since then. 

I hope three months doesn't sound too extreme? I just really want to do a good job with the showcase, and I've been pouring my heart into it. It's a good thing to be passionate about your work, right? I'm just trying to make the most of this opportunity, I promise. Does that make sense?
